Definition: Abda, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Abda is the name of two Israelites — one the father of Adoniram, who was over Solomon’s tribute, and the other ‘Abda the son of Shammua’, a Levite who served in Jerusalem after the return from exile. Two men, two centuries apart, both named in lists of servants.
TheologicalSignificance: A name in a list is easy to skip, but God does not skip names. I believe Abda matters because the Bible remembers servants: a tribute officer under Solomon and a Levite singer after the exile are both written down, and no faithful service is too small for God's record.
